mac_awake.mac_reference_basis: each patient's own age-adjusted MAC (Katoh 1993, slow washout, descending)

sources.citation: De Wolf AM, Van Zundert TC, De Cooman S, Hendrickx JF. Theoretical effect of hyperventilation on speed of recovery and risk of rehypnotization following recovery - a Gas Man simulation. BMC Anesthesiology. 2012;12:22.
sources.note: Tier 3, reference implementation (see docs/MODEL.md, 'Source hierarchy'). Table 1 reports the Gas Man sevoflurane blood:gas and tissue:gas coefficients used here. De Wolf et al. ran Gas Man simulations and measured no coefficient: Table 1 is the parameter set they supplied to it, so this is the Gas Man set carrying a journal's name rather than a measurement. It is the source of the stored values.

sources.citation: Strum DP, Eger EI II. Partition coefficients for sevoflurane in human blood, saline, and olive oil. Anesthesia & Analgesia. 1987;66(7):654-656.
sources.note: Tier 1, primary measurement, cited but not adopted. Human study reporting a blood:gas coefficient of 0.686 +/- 0.047 (mean +/- SD) at 37 degrees C in 19 ASA I-III patients aged 21-77. The stored value 0.65 is the Gas Man figure and is 5.2 percent lower. No primary source has been adopted for this parameter; PL-D6LX carries the decision.

sources.citation: Yasuda N, Targ AG, Eger EI II. Solubility of I-653, sevoflurane, isoflurane, and halothane in human tissues. Anesthesia & Analgesia. 1989;69(3):370-373.
sources.note: Tier 1, primary measurement, cited but not adopted. Human tissue study reporting a sevoflurane brain:blood partition coefficient of 1.70 +/- 0.09 at 37 degrees C. The stored tissue:gas values are Gas Man's; dividing vessel_rich by blood:gas gives an implied brain:blood of 1.1/0.65 = 1.692, 0.5 percent below Yasuda's measurement. Adopting the measured values is not a substitution: this model's vessel_rich group is a lumped compartment (brain, heart, liver, kidney, viscera) and Yasuda reports per-organ coefficients, so a group-weighting scheme would have to be constructed and justified. PL-D6LX carries that.

sources.citation: Drager Vapor 2000 Sevoflurane vaporizer specification: calibrated concentration range 0.2-8%.
sources.note: Manufacturer specification, and the primary source for a device capability: docs/MODEL.md's source hierarchy concerns measured physiologic quantities, and a calibrated dial maximum is not one. Standard variable-bypass sevoflurane vaporizer (e.g. Drager Vapor 2000, Datex-Ohmeda Sevotec 5) calibrated dial maximum, used here as max_delivered_concentration_percent. This is a device-capability limit on the delivered-concentration control, not a scientific model parameter; it does not affect the governing equations.

sources.citation: Nickalls RWD, Mapleson WW. Age-related iso-MAC charts for isoflurane, sevoflurane and desflurane in man. British Journal of Anaesthesia. 2003;91(2):170-174.
sources.note: The stored mac_percent is tier 3: it is the flat adult MAC De Wolf et al. state they used in their Gas Man simulations, not a value taken from this paper. Nickalls and Mapleson is cited but not adopted. It is tier 2, not tier 1 - its own abstract states the charts "are based on Mapleson's meta-analysis (1996) of the available MAC data", so it synthesises measurements rather than making one, and docs/MODEL.md's source hierarchy does not admit tier 2 as the authority for a stored value. It is also age-related, and this project's reference-adult model has no age parameter, so mac_percent uses the flat adult value from De Wolf et al. above (same paper already cited for partition coefficients: 'MAC values that we used in our Gas Man simulations are: desflurane 6%, sevoflurane 2%, isoflurane 1.2%'). Used as the controller's starting delivered-concentration default (1 MAC) and as the divisor of the interface's MAC-multiple display unit; it is not a governing-equation parameter and no equation in core/ reads it. See docs/MODEL.md, 'MAC multiples as a display unit' and 'Delivery-limit and MAC parameters'.

sources.citation: Mapleson WW. Effect of age on MAC in humans: a meta-analysis. British Journal of Anaesthesia. 1996;76(2):179-185.
sources.note: Tier 2, secondary synthesis, cited but not adopted; the source of the age-40 MAC this project's stored value is measured against. Regression of a comprehensive literature survey, reporting MAC at age 40 as 1.8 percent for sevoflurane (95% confidence limits about plus or minus 7 percent for isoflurane and sevoflurane and 10 percent for desflurane), and MAC falling about 6 percent per decade of age. The stored mac_percent of 2 percent is 11.1 percent higher. Not adopted for two reasons: a meta-analysis measures nothing and is tier 2 under docs/MODEL.md's source hierarchy, which admits only tier 1 as the authority for a stored value; and every other parameter in this model is the Gas Man set, so a Mapleson divisor over a Gas Man trajectory would make each displayed MAC multiple a ratio between two parameter lineages. The consequence is displayed and disclosed rather than silently absorbed: against this source the interface's MAC multiples for sevoflurane read 10 percent low, and because the sevoflurane and desflurane errors run in opposite directions a cross-agent comparison at '1 MAC' is displaced by about 22 percent. docs/MODEL.md, 'Known limitations', carries that; ROADMAP.md's planned-milestone item 31 is the route to primary values.

sources.citation: Katoh T, Suguro Y, Kimura T, Ikeda K. Cerebral awakening concentration of sevoflurane and isoflurane predicted during slow and fast alveolar washout. Anesthesia & Analgesia. 1993;77(5):1012-1017.
sources.note: Tier 1, primary measurement, and the source of the stored mac_awake. 49 ASA I patients; MAC-awake was determined as the average of the bracketing alveolar concentrations that allow and prevent response to verbal command during recovery, and reported "as a ratio to age-adjusted MAC". That ratio is what is stored: it is the form the paper reports, and the only form that stays correct if mac_percent is ever changed or made age-aware. Slow washout (concentration decreased in 15-minute steps, brain assumed equilibrated with alveolar gas) gave 0.34 +/- 0.05 for sevoflurane; fast washout (discontinuation from 0.5 MAC) gave 0.22 +/- 0.07 MAC, significantly smaller, and the paper attributes the difference to end-tidal-to-arterial and arterial-to-cerebral anesthetic differences - which is what this model represents as the alveolar-to-vessel-rich difference. The slow-washout figure is the one stored because it is the *brain* concentration at awakening, and the paper measures that directly rather than leaving it to inference: cerebral concentration at first eye opening during fast washout was 0.34 +/- 0.08 MAC, "nearly equal to MAC-Awake obtained by slow alveolar washout". That is why docs/MODEL.md requires the band to be read against the vessel-rich trace. Determination is descending (during washout); the desflurane value in desflurane.json is ascending, and the two are not interchangeable methods. Retrieved from PubMed (PMID 8214700) and verified against the abstract 2026-09-04.
